Starts the level: waits for the raster, blanks the screen, selects VIC-II bank 1 ($4000), unpacks the picture (colour, screen at $5C00 and bitmap at $6000) from $9D90, points the raster call at level_raster ($81BE) and sets the VIC-II from the list after the call.
The JSR's high byte; the BCC the disassembler once saw here is an artefact.
unpack_inline's arguments: the packed data at $9D90 ($9D90), 2918 bytes long.
The packed picture's length, 2,918 bytes.
Points the raster call at level_raster.

Text goes to the bitmap at $6000 (text_origin), the object tables are linked, the seven objects made and the four marines placed (marines_init), the motion tracker cleared (tracker_clear); then the screen comes on.

Once every two frames: checks for the end, runs the current marine (marine_tick), the sound and the motion tracker (aliens_tick), moves the marine, its gun flash and the three aliens, sorts the sprites, then on alternate passes redraws the tracker and one pair of monitors, or the other pair.
The end is checked every pass (check_end). It has to hold for 55 passes in a row ($0606): a pass where it fails starts the count again.
$0602 counts down to a redraw of the room after the current marine has died.
Waits for frame 1 of the pass (the engine's frame counter $020D, cleared at the top).
Remembers the key pressed this pass ($0221) for marine_switch.
Waits for frame 2, then goes round again.
The end: shows the marines in the APC, prints how many returned ("n RETURNED", the digit at $9385) and waits about 165 passes, keeping the monitors alive, then jumps to the engine's stage_complete.
Inside level_end: the trainer pokes $8139 when it loads level 6, whose code lies here then.
Inside level_end: the trainer pokes $813A when it loads level 6, whose code lies here then.
Inside level_end: the trainer pokes $813B when it loads level 6, whose code lies here then.

Counts the marines dead ($0603, state $FF), caught ($0604, state 2) and in the APC ($0605, state 4); any other state returns with the carry clear. With every marine dead or in the APC, returns with the carry set. With every marine dead or caught, clears bits 4-7 of the marines byte $0204 (all four lost) and sets the carry.
Stores the count of caught marines.
The raster call at line $FB: level_frame, sprites in front of the background, and a second raster call at line $64 (raster_split), then a random number.
At line $64, the split below the room view: puts back the sprite priorities from the engine's copy and the raster call at line $FB.
For level_end: picks the marines in the APC to show.

Gives the hardware sprites to the marines in the current marine's room and, with fewer than two of them, to the three aliens, sorted by their y so that nearer ones are drawn in front: up to four objects, their parts to the sprite slots from $937D.
Hands each object's two parts their sprite slots.

Draws the view of room X. The room's byte in room_map gives its exits; the APC ($BE), room $56 and one more are special views. The exits pick a view (0-31), and the view's four quarters are drawn with draw_char_block, each from its own font and character list: top left at $6000, top right at $6058, bottom left at $6780, bottom right at $67D8.
X is the view number from here on.

Sets the room view's 22 by 12 screen cells to mid grey and dark grey ($CB) and their colour RAM to light grey ($0F).
The colour RAM value, $0F.

Plots a blip at column X, row Y into the tracker's image: the row's address from $99E6/$99EC, the bits ANDed with one of four random shapes from $99C6, so the blip flickers.
Clears the tracker's image buffer ($9755-$9A25) and draws its grid back from the list at $96B3 (bytes) and $9704 (where they go).
The high byte of the store's address, stepped on by tracker_clear.

Makes the seven objects (types from $9A17: four marines and three aliens), puts each marine in a random room (random_room) at the position and facing from $9A1E-$9A26, with its timer from $9A32, and the aliens hidden.
monitor_static reads 40 bytes from here, from a random offset, for a monitor's first row of static: the level's own code serves as noise.
The STA that sets each marine's facing; its bytes, like those at $8488 and $84D8, are read by monitor_static as noise.
The source of the third row of static, more of the level's code.
Starts with Drake (marine 0) on the monitors and draws his room.
The current marine: marine_switch, the timers (marines_timers), then, unless he is dead or caught, the joystick moves him through the room and its exits (marine_move); fire shoots (marine_fire).
The joystick's directions ($0222) give the facing from $99F2; fire held keeps the facing, so the marine can back away while firing.
Walking animation on while the marine moves, stopped on its first frame when he stands.
Footsteps: sfx_crash plays at each step of the walk.
start_effect's argument: $3526 (sfx_crash).
Keeps the part number.
Between y $34 and $3F the marine is behind the room's furniture: the priority bit is set on his parts.
Updates who is where (marines_group).
Works out how far the marine may walk in the room at his depth y: left and right edges $84/$83 and the doorways' edges $86/$85.
Moving right: at the right doorway ($81 bit 1) he leaves through it into the next room (room + 1); otherwise he stops at the wall.
Moving left: through the left doorway ($81 bit 3) into room - 1.
Moving down: through the front doorway ($81 bit 2) into room + 16, arriving at the back.
Otherwise he stops at the front wall.
Moving up: through the back doorway ($81 bit 0) into room - 16, arriving at the front.

Turns the marine to face his direction of travel ($80): sets his gun part's offset and frame animation.
Inside marine_face: the trainer pokes $8854 when it loads level 3, whose code lies here then.

Fire: shows the gun flash (part 1 of the marine) for $060A passes (6 on PAL, 5 on NTSC), plays sfx_burst and works out the hit (fire_hit). Not while the marine is caught, or under attack but not yet seen.
start_effect's argument: $34AF (sfx_burst).

Inside room_redraw: the trainer pokes $88B5 when it loads level 6, whose code lies here then.

Called as a marine leaves a room. Under attack with aliens in sight, he cannot shake them off: the attack goes on in the next room (attack_follow). With no alien in sight he escapes: the attack ends and his next attack is set by his kills ($9A36).

Marines in the same room keep together (state 3), and a marine in the APC room $BE is safe (state 4). A marine who is alone again goes back to state 0 with at least ten ticks of $020B before his next attack.
Picks a random room that is on the map, is not the APC and has no marine in it.
F1, F3, F5 and F7 ($0221 = 0-3) switch the monitors to another marine, unless the current one is under attack. Redraws the tracker, the room and, if he is under attack or caught, the aliens.
Shows the current marine's key and name ("1:DRAKE"), the name from the engine's marine_names in capitals, at $9A47.

Each marine's timer ($060B, in ticks of $020B, about 1.2 seconds on PAL). State 0: when it runs out an attack starts (state 1): 16 aliens to kill ($060F), a grace of 40 ($0627) and an alarm. Under attack and not on the monitors, each tick an alien may die (random under $96) or the marine is caught (random $E0 or more). On the monitors he is caught when his grace runs out.
The BCS's offset, 8, to the catch at $8A92. The trainer's level 2 cheat writes 3, so an unseen marine is never caught at random: the branch goes to the grace check at $8A8D instead.
Caught (state 2): he is dead when the timer, set by his kills, runs out.
Dead (state $FF): his bit in the marines byte $0204 is cleared ($9A5B). If he was on the monitors, the room goes black and is redrawn 55 passes later.
Shows the current marine caught: in the middle of the room, with the aliens round him (aliens_place).
Scatters the tracker's blips for an attack: each comes from a random open direction of the room, at a random column and row.
The number of blips, written by attack_start.
Scatters the blips again for an attack that follows the marine into a new room.
The number of blips, written by attack_follow.
